title: Training Philosophy
description: A source's non-negotiable guiding principles. Governs what the system will and won't do when drawing from this methodology.

id.description: Unique slug. Used as reference key across the system. e.g. 'starting_strength', 'uphill_athlete'

name.description: Human-readable name. e.g. 'Starting Strength / Mark Rippetoe'

core_principles.description: Non-negotiable beliefs expressed as short slug strings. These are the axioms — the system won't violate them when this source is active.

scope.description: Which modalities this philosophy claims authority over. Use existing modality IDs or introduce new ones specific to this package (e.g. 'swimming', 'cycling', 'contact_strength').

bias.description: Modalities this philosophy actively emphasizes. Subset of scope.

avoid_with.description: Modality IDs this philosophy conflicts with at high volume. Can reference any installed modality ID.

required_equipment.description: Equipment that must be present for this philosophy to be applicable. If missing, system cannot draw from this source.

intensity_model.description: How this philosophy approaches intensity across the week.

progression_philosophy.description: Primary mechanism by which this source defines progress.

sources.description: Source documents or URLs this entry was derived from.

notes.description: Free-text notes, known gaps, or caveats about this entry.

primary_track_id.description: Default track. When omitted the first track is the default.

id.description: Track id, unique within this philosophy.

name.description: Display name for the track (what the athlete picks in the builder).

description.description: What this track is for and when to choose it.

id.description: Phase id, unique within its track. The philosophy's own name for the phase.

name.description: Display name, in the philosophy's own words.

kind.description: Shared phase kind (data/commons/phase_kinds.yaml) the engine keys on: archetype applicable_phases, volume multipliers, cadence, taper filter, analytics deload reading.

framework_id.description: Framework that builds this phase's weeks. Must be one of this package's frameworks.

focus.description: One-line focus shown on the phase.

description.description: What this phase is and why, in the philosophy's own terms. Shown on the program overview.

repeatable.description: A block that may be cycled (run again) rather than a one-off step.

priority_override.description: Optional modality priority adjustments for this phase.

checks.description: What the phase's prose says, in a form tools/check_fidelity.py can test a generated program against. Only what no framework field already carries; the generator never reads it.

archetypes_required.description: Each archetype id must appear in every non-deload week of the phase.

archetypes_forbidden.description: Archetype ids that must never appear in the phase.

exercises_forbidden.description: Exercise ids that must never appear in the phase (a lift the method has not reached yet).

modalities_required.description: Modalities that must appear in every non-deload week of the phase.

fixed_exercises.description: Loaded main lifts keep their exercise across the phase (true), or rotate by design (false). Default: true unless the philosophy's intensity_model is constant_variation.

max_zone.description: Highest heart-rate zone any aerobic or interval slot may prescribe in this phase.

volume_change_per_week.description: [min, max] fractional change in planned minutes from one non-deload week to the next within the phase.

volume_vs_previous_phase.description: [min, max] fractional change of this phase's mean weekly minutes against the previous phase's last non-deload week.

intensity_split_tolerance.description: Largest share-point deviation from the framework's intensity_distribution in any bucket (default 0.15).

tracks.description: Ways to follow this philosophy. Each track is an ordered list of the philosophy's own phases; each phase names its framework and a shared kind. Replaces framework_groups and canonical_phase_sequence.

self_contained.description: When true, generation may only use this package and any package listed in borrows_from. Sessions that cannot be filled are reported as coverage gaps instead of being taken from another philosophy.

borrows_from.description: Packages this philosophy explicitly draws on. Borrowed sessions are labelled in the UI.

label.description: Display name for the "via X" badge.

reason.description: Why this philosophy legitimately draws on that one.

modalities.description: Modalities the borrow covers. Omit or ['*'] for any.

kinds.description: What may be taken from the borrowed package. Defaults to both. ['exercises'] borrows the movements while keeping this philosophy's own session designs.

expectations.description: Aggregate program expectations across the whole philosophy (weeks, days/week, session minutes).
